- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) within 3–5 days, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract sentiment-driven downward bias.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative after a peak; apply a 1–2 day lead correction to anticipate reversal.
- In 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values to reduce noise-driven overcorrection.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.5), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 10-day mean to anchor forecast.
